4. Issue notice.

The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 11.07.2020 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife Sachin Bansal & Ors vs State & Anr on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46516203/

sentences.text: Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 03.10.2020.
On 12.12.2020, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement Agreement dated 22.09.2022 arrived before Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District, Delhi.
A copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13B(2) of the HMA was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 23.11.2022 passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, , Rohini Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, , Rohini Delhi
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
7. Petitioner nos. 1, 3 and 4 and respondent no.2 are present in Court and petitioner no. 2 is appearing through video conferencing.
Parties have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, Rs. 6,00,000/- has been transferred to bank account of respondent no. 2 through RTGS (RTGS -AUBLR 620231017- This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/10/2023 at 21:31:43 1040447).
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
8. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
9. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No. 332/2020,
under Sections 498A/406/427/509/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Budh Vihar, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
10.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
